statement: A point $P$ is chosen uniformly at random inside a cube of edge length $2$. What is the probability that $P$ is closer to the center of the cube than to every one of the cube's eight vertices?

choices.misconception: I took the region to be the octahedron |x| + |y| + |z| <= 1 through the face centers, whose volume 4/3 is 1/6 of the cube.
I thought the region was the ball of radius sqrt(3)/2, half the distance from the center to a vertex.
I found the octahedron |x| + |y| + |z| <= 3/2 with volume 9/2, but took each of the six tips outside the cube to have volume 1/6 instead of 1/12.
I found the octahedron |x| + |y| + |z| <= 3/2 but did not cut off the six tips that stick out through the faces of the cube.

hints: Put the center at the origin, so the vertices are $(\pm1, \pm1, \pm1)$.

Being closer to the origin than to a vertex $v$ means lying on the origin's side of the plane that perpendicularly bisects the segment from the origin to $v$. Combine all eight conditions into one inequality.
The eight conditions are $\pm x \pm y \pm z < \frac32$, which together say $|x| + |y| + |z| < \frac32$: an octahedron. Find its volume and remove the parts outside the cube.

solutions.reliable: With the center at the origin, $P = (x, y, z)$ is closer to the origin than to $(1,1,1)$ when $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 < (x-1)^2 + (y-1)^2 + (z-1)^2$, that is, $x + y + z < \frac32$. All eight vertices together give $|x| + |y| + |z| < \frac32$, an octahedron of volume $\frac43\left(\frac32\right)^3 = \frac92$. It pokes out through each face of the cube: the part with $x > 1$ is a pyramid with apex $(\frac32, 0, 0)$, height $\frac12$ and base the square $|y| + |z| \le \frac12$ of area $\frac12$, so its volume is $\frac13 \cdot \frac12 \cdot \frac12 = \frac1{12}$. Removing six tips leaves $\frac92 - \frac12 = 4$, half of the cube's volume $8$. The probability is $\frac12$. Transferable idea: 'closer to A than to B' is a half-space bounded by the perpendicular bisector plane.
solutions.elegant: Cut the cube into eight unit cubes, one at each vertex. In the unit cube $[0,1]^3$, the binding condition is $x + y + z < \frac32$, since the other seven conditions are weaker there. The point reflection $(x, y, z) \mapsto (1-x, 1-y, 1-z)$ maps this unit cube to itself and swaps $x + y + z < \frac32$ with $x + y + z > \frac32$, so exactly half of each unit cube qualifies.
